scenes.visual: Portrait pushes in slowly; name and dates appear.

scenes.tts: Gerty Cori was the daughter of a sugar-refinery manager, an irony she savored, and she compressed eight years of Latin and five of science into a single year to pass an entrance exam built to keep women out.
scenes.visual: Gerty: refinery manager's daughter; eight years of Latin + five of science -> one year; exam
scenes.narration: Gerty Cori was the daughter of a sugar-refinery manager, an irony she savored, and she compressed eight years of Latin and five of science into a single year to pass an entrance exam built to keep women out.

scenes.tts: Told by an institute director to stop publishing with her husband — two married people sharing a byline was not how things were done — she refused, and out of that refusal came the work that mapped how glycogen is stored and mobilized: glycogen phosphorylase, the glucose-1-phosphate "Cori ester," and the Cori cycle that shuttles lactate from muscle to liver and glucose back.
scenes.visual: Institute director orders no joint publishing; she refused; glycogen stored/mobilized; phosphorylase, Cori ester, Cori cycle

scenes.tts: When the 1947 Nobel arrived, Carl insisted the prize was as much hers, and Gerty became the first woman to win the Nobel in Medicine.
